Report_ID: Self-reported improvement in constipation (improvement rate / improvement cases)
Title: Probiotics for constipation and gut microbiota in Parkinson's disease
Author: Du et al.
Comment: Table 1 column order is Control then Probiotics; counts assigned accordingly (control 2/23, probiotics 12/23). Totals are randomized N (BOCF used for 3 dropouts). Paper does not itself report a risk ratio, so the ratio field was left empty.
Participant type: Idiopathic Parkinson's disease patients with functional constipation (Rome III)
Recruitment source: Beijing Friendship Hospital, Capital Medical University
Outcome measurement: Number of participants classified as improved out of total randomized per arm
Outcome variable: Self-reported improvement in constipation (improvement rate / improvement cases)
additional_group_ns: 30 sex- and age-matched healthy controls included for microbiota comparison only; not part of this comparison

Report_ID: Self-reported improvement in constipation (no longer <3 bowel movements/week at 8 weeks)
Title: Multi-strain probiotics (Hexbio) containing MCP BCMC strains improved constipation and gut motility in Parkinson's disease: A randomised controlled trial
Author: Ibrahim A, Ali RAR, Manaf MRA, Ahmad N, Tajurruddin FW, Qin WZ, Desa SHM, Mohamed Ibrahim N
Comment: Events recorded are participants IMPROVED (no longer <3 BM/week), derived by subtracting the paper's reported still-constipated counts from each arm total (22 and 26) — the paper itself reports only the still-constipated counts (5 and 15) and an odds ratio of 0.22 (95% CI 0.06, 0.76) for HAVING <3 BM/week, i.e. the inverse direction. Denominators are completers analysed at 8 weeks (22 and 26), not the numbers randomised (27 and 28); the authors state ITT could only be performed for the gut transit time outcome. This subanalysis was post hoc (not part of the initial study design). No risk ratio is reported by the paper, so the ratio fields are left empty.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Multi-strain probiotic (Hexbio, MCP BCMC, 30x10^9 CFU + 2% FOS) twice daily, 8 weeks') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Idiopathic Parkinson's disease patients with functional constipation (Rome III), Hoehn & Yahr 1–4
Recruitment source: Parkinson's and neurology outpatient clinic, Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz, UKM Medical Centre, Kuala Lumpur
Outcome measurement: Number of patients per arm who no longer reported <3 BM/week at 8 weeks, derived as arm total minus the reported number with BM <3 times/week (probiotic 22-5=17; placebo 26-15=11)
Outcome variable: Self-reported improvement in constipation (no longer <3 bowel movements/week at 8 weeks)

Report_ID: Self-reported improvement in constipation: increase in CBMs >=1 during weeks 3 and 4 (% of patients / treatment responders)
Title: Probiotics and prebiotic fiber for constipation associated with Parkinson disease: An RCT
Author: Barichella M, Pacchetti C, Bolliri C, Cassani E, Iorio L, Pusani C, Pinelli G, Privitera G, Cesari I, Faierman SA, Caccialanza R, Pezzoli G, Cereda E
Comment: Event counts are NOT reported verbatim; they were derived from the paper's explicitly stated percentages applied to the explicitly stated randomized group sizes (53.8% x 80 = 43.0; 25.0% x 40 = 10). Also note an internal discrepancy: the Abstract reports OR 3.5, 95% CI 1.8-8.1 for this same endpoint, while Table 3 reports OR 3.4, 95% CI 1.5-8.0 (Table 3 value extracted). Percentages come from an ITT analysis with multiple imputation for 5 dropouts.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Experimental group: fermented milk with multiple probiotic strains + prebiotic fiber') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: randomized controlled trial (double-blind, placebo-controlled, 2:1 parallel group)
Participant type: outpatients with idiopathic Parkinson disease and Rome III-confirmed functional constipation
Recruitment source: tertiary single-center Parkinson disease outpatient clinic (165 screened, 120 randomized), June-October 2015
Outcome measurement: Proportion of randomized patients reporting an increase of one or more CBMs per week during weeks 3 and 4 (intention-to-treat, multiple imputation)
Outcome variable: Self-reported improvement in constipation: increase in CBMs >=1 during weeks 3 and 4 (% of patients / treatment responders)

Report_ID: Self-reported improvement in constipation (proportion reporting satisfaction with intervention regarding improvement in constipation)
Title: Probiotics for constipation in Parkinson's disease: A randomized placebo-controlled study
Author: Tan, Ai Huey
Comment: Event counts are NOT reported verbatim — only percentages. The stated percentages do not correspond to the randomized denominators (65.6% x 34 = 22.3; 21.6% x 38 = 8.2) but do correspond exactly to the completers (21/32 = 65.6%; 8/37 = 21.6%), so the denominator for this outcome is ambiguous; no event counts were entered to avoid inventing numbers. P reported as "P<0.001" and entered as 0.001 (upper bound). Chi-square test statistic not reported.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Multi-strain probiotics capsule (10 billion CFU, 8 strains), once daily for 4 weeks') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); unsupported or insufficient statistic type
Participant type: Patients aged >=40 years with Parkinson's disease fulfilling Rome IV criteria for functional constipation
Recruitment source: Neurology Outpatient Clinic, University of Malaya Medical Centre, Kuala Lumpur
Outcome measurement: Proportion of patients reporting satisfaction with intervention received
Outcome variable: Self-reported improvement in constipation (proportion reporting satisfaction with intervention regarding improvement in constipation)
